ssh_bruteforce.description: Adversaries use automated tools to guess account passwords by repeatedly attempting different password values against one or more accounts, typically without prior knowledge of valid credentials.
common_indicators: Many failed login attempts from a single source in a short time
Repeated attempts against the same username
Connection resets/reconnects after hitting authentication limits
recommended_response: Verify whether the target account's password was eventually compromised (check for a success after the failures)
Block or rate-limit the source IP at the firewall
Consider enforcing key-based SSH authentication instead of passwords
Review whether fail2ban or similar intrusion-prevention tooling is active

port_scan.description: Adversaries attempt to get a listing of services running on remote hosts, including those that may be vulnerable to remote software exploitation, typically as reconnaissance before a more targeted attack.
common_indicators: Many different destination ports probed from a single source IP
Probes occurring in a very short time window (seconds)
Traffic to ports with no legitimate service (e.g. rarely-used or uncommon ports)
recommended_response: Identify what the scan revealed (which ports responded vs. were filtered)
Confirm no unnecessary services are exposed on probed ports
Monitor the source IP for follow-up activity, which often indicates scanning was reconnaissance for a targeted attack
Consider blocking the source IP if scanning is clearly hostile and not expected traffic
